Reference.Title: RAU-Net3D: a two-stage deep learning method for pneumothorax volume assessment with three-dimensional electrical impedance tomography
Reference.Address: [Li, Zhiwei; Wu, Hongtao; Liu, Kai] Nanjing Univ Aeronaut & Astronaut, Coll Mech & Elect Engn, Nanjing 210000, Peoples R China; [Wu, Yang] Nanjing Forestry Univ, Coll Mech & Elect Engn, Nanjing 210037, Peoples R China; [Qi, Chen] Nanjing Univ, Jinling Hosp, Affiliated Hosp,Med Sch, Dept Cardiothorac Surg, Nanjing, Peoples R China; [Wang, Hao; Tian, He] Jinan Univ, Affiliated Hosp 1, Dept Anesthesiol, Guangzhou 510000, Peoples R China; [Wang, Hao; Tian, He] Jinan Univ, Affiliated Hosp 1, Clin Res Inst, Guangzhou 510000, Peoples R China; [Xie, Yu] Jinan Univ, Affiliated Hosp 6, Dongguan 523576, Peoples R China; [Yao, Jiafeng] Jinan Univ, Coll Phys & Optoelect Engn, Guangzhou 510632, Peoples R China
Reference.Abstract: A two-stage deep learning method is proposed to quantitatively infer pleural gas and compressed lung regions from dynamic three-dimensional electrical impedance tomography (3D EIT) based on the RAU-Net3D network architecture. The RAU-Net3D model integrates 3D residual connections and 3D attention mechanisms within a 3D U-Net framework, effectively enhancing feature extraction and segmentation of pneumothorax regions. In the first stage, time-differential voltage data are pre-reconstructed into a coarse 3D ventilation pixel matrix using the 3D GREIT algorithm. In the second stage, the RAU-Net3D network establishes an end-to-end mapping from the 3D ventilation pixel matrix to the corresponding 3D CT pixel matrix. A total of 7380 training datasets were constructed using CT scans from 150 subjects with intact lungs and 60 patients diagnosed with pneumothorax. The proposed method was validated through a series of ablation experiments and human experiments, demonstrating significant advantages in pneumothorax localization and volume quantification. In the single-time-point measurements for three pneumothorax patients, the RAU-Net3D model achieved relative volume errors of 10.20 %, 11.31 %, and 8.36 % in pneumothorax detection compared to CT. During a dynamic monitoring experiment, the RAU-Net3D model achieved relative volume errors of 0.76 % and 4.48 % for the pre-drainage and postoperative stages compared to CT, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of the model for noninvasive, radiation-free assessment of pneumothorax in dynamic bedside environments.
